title: Service-lane escrow: quota-aware handoff & soft-handoff for free→paid→enterprise
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: tenant requests should prefer lower-cost (free) lanes when available but must fall back to paid/enterprise variants without surprising failures or big latency spikes when quotas are near depletion. We need a deterministic, observable, and testable mechanism to: (1) prefer free lane while respecting quotas, (2) gracefully transition to paid/enterprise when quota thresholds are hit or expected to be hit soon, and (3) bias regional selection to reduce cross-region penalty while preserving SLA for higher tiers.

This ticket implements a "service-lane escrow" concept: short-lived escrow reservations and soft-handoff windows that let the router transition traffic between lanes with minimal tail-latency and transparent billing behaviour. The approach combines quota forecasting, small escrow reservations, and policy-driven demotion/handoff.

Non-goals: building a full billing engine, changing plan definitions, or reworking model-variant compatibility logic (we assume model variants have already been mapped in model-catalog).
acceptance_criteria: Router supports escrow-reservations: SLO for reserve allocation < 10ms in 95th percentile under normal load
Requests routed to free lane until escrow threshold is reached and then routed to paid lane without connection failures > 0.1% over 24h in canary region
Handoff window allows in-flight KV/cache reuse between lanes for compatible model variants with < 15% increase in token latency average during transition
Dashboard exposes per-tenant: escrow usage, handoff events, forecasted quota burn, and routed lane distribution
Automated e2e tests validate quota-breach → soft-handoff → paid routing and verify correct billing flag in request metadata
tech_notes: Escrow model: when a request arrives we attempt an escrow reserve of X tokens from tenant quota (configurable per-plan). If reserve accepted, route to free lane. If rejected or forecast predicts depletion within W seconds, route to paid lane immediately.
Forecast: use short-window exponential smoothing over recent token burn (default 30s) + burst allowance. Forecast must run in O(1) per tenant and be cacheable across routers.

Graceful handoff: implement 3-phase handoff - PREPARE (mark request with handoff_intent), ESCROW_LOCK (temporary reservation on candidate target lane), CUTOVER (new requests go to target, in-flight continue; after drain period, release old lane resources).

Regional affinity: prefer lane in same region when latency delta < threshold; otherwise penalize cross-region option based on SLA and cost policy. Region selection runs after escrow decision to avoid double work.

Model variant fallback: maintain compatibility matrix. If free lane's variant incompatible with paid lane, router will attempt a fast model-translation path (if available) or skip escrow and route to most compatible paid variant.
Storage: escrow state stored in a small sharded in-memory store keyed by tenant, with durable fallback to Redis for longer holds. TTL short (default 10s) to avoid long-lived reservations.
Observability: emit events for escrow_attempt, escrow_granted, escrow_rejected, handoff_start, handoff_cutover, handoff_complete with tenant, region, lane, and forecasted_burn tags.
Safety: rate-limit escrow attempts per-tenant to avoid storms during traffic spikes. Use circuit-breaker to fall back to conservative routing when forecast component misbehaves.
rollout_steps: 1) Implement escrow/forecast lib behind a feature flag in router (canary disabled)
2) Unit tests + integration tests in staging; validate forecast accuracy and no global CPU regressions
3) Enable feature flag for 1% of traffic in us-west-2 (canary), monitor alerts for latency and error spikes for 48h
4) Increase to 10% with adjustments (if no regressions) and test cross-region latency behavior
5) Gradual rollout to all regions + enable per-tenant opt-in UI in Console (start with beta customers)
6) GA release after 2 weeks of stable metrics and PM signoff
testing_plan: Unit tests for escrow state machine and forecast heuristics (edge cases: zero-traffic, sudden spike, sustained burn)
Integration: synthetic traffic that simulates quota exhaustion patterns (steady burn, spiky bursts, diurnal) and assert soft-handoff behavior
E2E: canary tenant with known quota limits; verify billing metadata tag when routing to paid lane
Chaos: introduce router process restarts and Redis latency to validate escrow TTL handling and no double-charge conditions
Performance: benchmarks ensuring escrow decision < 1% added p99 latency compared to baseline under 50% load
updates: 2026-03-10: Asha created ticket and sketched initial state machine. Forecast approach chosen (exp smoothing) after sync with Applied ML.
2026-03-11: Design review with Runtime team — decided on in-memory sharded escrow store with Redis fallback. Liam volunteered to own implementation.
2026-03-12: PM requested per-tenant opt-in and Console flag; added rollout step and dashboard requirement.
2026-03-13: Implementation branch opened (router feature flag + lib). Started writing unit tests for forecast component. Planning canary in us-west-2.
open_questions: What should default escrow size be for free plans (tokens vs request-count)?
Tolerance window for forecasting false positives (how conservative should we be to avoid premature cutover)?
Do we expose handoff events to customers in Console or only internal metrics?
Is it acceptable to allocate temporary paid capacity on cutover when billing reconciliation lags?
